description: Base 7: copy Base 4 (voice-b7260e73) with Handle 7 (voice-448df859) and simplify significantly, with a focus on 3D printability. The gripper fingers are pretty good; the other pieces are too complex and not very printable. Every piece should print on an FDM printer without supports, ideally: flat bases, overhangs at 45° or less, no floating features, sensible split lines, and a print orientation noted for each part. Fewer parts. Keep it parameterized and driven by the single RobStride RS00. Rejected approaches: Base 5 (voice-01ab1486, single-gear) and Base 6 (voice-0973c464) — do not build on them.

results.identified_issue: Rule used: every printed part is a stack of Y-extrusions, each no wider than the one below. That's checked on exports/print meshes by face normal (overhang = asin(-n_z) > 45.5 deg above z 0) plus mesh components == 1. hub_top was raised from 0 to 14 because Base 4's hub was cut at the pivot, which left half the post bore open under the finger. genus showed it (bore merged into the gap). The handle grew to 15.2 because the plate must reach the bed face. The alternative was printing the handle-gear top-down, but then the pocket floor becomes a large bridge. Rejected: fusing fingers into the handle-gears (breaks the separate Gripper/Handle/Base modularity and the colours; offered to Jake instead), a 2-screw base (kept 3 for torque), and anything from Base 5/6. Not verified: slicing, real clearances, post wear/wobble (3 mm bearing), screw engagement (computed only: pinion 4.5 mm, base 4.3 mm). check_gripper_closure.py flags v307 'never touches' exactly as it does Base 1-4 and Handles 3-7 (pre-existing, same numbers).
results.summary: Base 7: Base 4 redrawn so every part prints flat without supports, with an automatic overhang check
results.detailed_description:
Base 7 is in v307_generalist_printable. It keeps Base 4's layout: two handle-gears in the finger plane, a centred pinion on the RS00 and a base plate. Gripper 21's fingers are unchanged.

Every printed part is now a flat 2D outline extruded straight up, so it lies on one face with vertical walls. The only slopes are the fingers' taper and 45° screw cones. Print orientations:
- Fingers: flat ventral face down.
- Handle-gears: web face down, finger pocket open on top.
- Pinion: teeth face down, spigot on top.
- Base: underside down, posts up.
exports/print/*.stl already lie on the bed that way. check_geometry.py now fails any face that overhangs past 45° and any part that isn't one solid sitting on the bed. All 6 printed parts have zero overhang. As a control, the pinion turned spigot-down shows about 1,350 mm² of overhang, so the check does catch them. All 42 checks pass.

What changed. Base 4's handle-gear was the problem: its teeth, handle plate and axle each started at a different height, so part of it always floated.
- Plate, strap boss, tail, hub and teeth now all run the full height.
- A post on the base replaces each axle, and the handle-gear turns on it.
- The hub is a full disc, so the post bears all the way round.
- The pinion's and base's M3 screws are countersunk on 45° cones. That's one screw type: M3x20 for the pinion, M3x10 for the base.

Two trade-offs:
- The handle is 15.2 mm edge-on instead of Handle 7's 12. The extra 3.2 mm is the floor under the finger, all on the ventral side, and it's the cost of a flat bottom.
- Each post bears over only 3 mm (web_t). Raising web_t lengthens the bearing but makes the handle taller.

Part count is still 13: 6 printed, the RS00 and 6 M3. I couldn't go lower without the pinion (Base 6) or a different drive (Base 5). The one real cut left is printing each finger into its handle-gear: 4 printed parts, 11 pieces, but each side would be one colour and the fingers couldn't be swapped. Want that as Base 8?

Nothing has been sliced or printed. The overhang check is geometry only.

summary: Base 7 should simplify Base 4 with Handle 7 into fewer parts, keeping the gripper fingers but redesigning the rest. Every part must print on FDM without supports, with a noted orientation, staying parameterized and driven by the single RS00.
